subject: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@therahealth.com>, Theresa Gomez <t.gomez@therahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance

Alex / Theresa —

Thanks for the sync earlier. Per our MAP discussion, attaching the working MAP spreadsheet (therahealth_mpa_v1.xlsx) — version 1 with deliverables, owners, and an activation timeline. Below is the slice that matters for the POC environment activation so we have a single place to drive to close: 

1) Org setup & API keys
   - Redwood: create customer org (org-id will be provided) — owner: Jordan (ETA 4/4)
   - TheraHealth: confirm list of service accounts and desired key TTLs
   - Acceptance: successful token-based call to /v1/generate in staging

2) IP allowlist
   - TheraHealth to provide CIDR(s) to allow (public egress IPs) — template: network_allowlist_template.csv
   - Redwood to confirm NAT IPs and provide final allowlist by EOD 4/4
   - Acceptance: outbound connectivity to our runtime on port 443 from allowed CIDRs

3) VPC peering (optional for private traffic)
   - If you want peering instead of IP allowlist -> we need VPC IDs, routing table owners, and a 2-hr peering window
   - Redwood ops will provision peering on our side; TheraHealth must accept the request

4) Timeline & close criteria
   - Proposed peering window: Tue 4/7 02:00–04:00 PDT (low traffic)
   - Sanity checks and test vectors run by TheraHealth within 24h of peering completion
   - Final acceptance = passing smoke tests + signed SLAs / DocuSign (link will be shared)

Next steps: can you confirm the IPs you will allow and whether you prefer peering? Also confirm the list of service accounts for key provisioning so I can issue ephemeral keys for testing.

Attachments: therahealth_mpa_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook)

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@therahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Theresa Gomez <t.gomez@therahealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 11:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the MAP workbook. Quick answers from our side: 

- We prefer VPC peering for the POC (security and observability reasons) but can fall back to IP allowlist if peering hits compliance gates.
- I'll send our VPC details in a separate email to your ops alias (vpc-id, account-number, routing contact).
- For API keys: we'll want short-lived service account keys for the initial smoke test (48h TTL).

Can you drop the network_allowlist_template.csv (sample) into the shared Drive so our infra team has it for the fallback path? Also, please include the DocuSign link for the SLA so legal can review in parallel.

I'll aim to have VPC details and the internal routing owner by EOD 4/4. If peering looks doable, 4/7 window sounds ok; we generally prefer the earlier slot (02:00–04:00 PDT).

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Platform Ops, TheraHealth
alex.rivera@therahealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@therahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance

Alex —

Perfect — thanks. I've uploaded the network_allowlist_template.csv to the shared folder and added the DocuSign SLA (docusign-therahealth-sla.pdf) for parallel review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/thera-mpa

Operational notes for the peering path: 
- Redwood requires: VPC ID (us-west-2), account ID, a CIDR range for the peering subnet, and the routing table owner (so we can populate routes on acceptance).
- We'll initiate the peering request from our account once you confirm the VPC ID; your infra team will accept and we'll validate routes.
- During the 2-hr window we will: create peering, push route entries, validate BGP-less connectivity, run TLS handshake + baseline requests (we'll provide test tokens).

I added a small row in the MAP workbook under "Peering Runbook" with the checklist steps so your infra owner can follow it. If the peering window on 4/7 is confirmed, Redwood ops will reserve the slot and publish a join URL for the runbook.

Attachment: network_allowlist_template.csv (sample)

Best —
Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@therahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance

Alex / Jordan —

Looping in a quick security preflight checklist so TheraHealth knows what evidence we'll need for the POC review: 

- Confirmed logging (request: examples of IPs/service account ids that will call API)
- Data residency: confirm that test data will not include PHI — if it does, we need the data handling approval route before peering
- SOC2-related artifacts: a short checklist is attached in the MAP workbook (Operational Controls > Evidence required)

If you prefer, Redwood security can run a 30-min preflight on Friday (4/9) morning to validate allowlist/peering config before the production window. That reduces back-and-forth during the peering slot.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@therahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: TheraHealth POC — environment activation & acceptance

Thanks, team —

All good from TheraHealth: peering window confirmed for Tue 4/7 02:00–04:00 PDT. Our infra owner (Teresa Gomez) will accept the peering request and run the routing changes.

Action items we completed this morning: 
- VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e (us-west-2) — routing owner: Theresa Gomez (t.gomez@therahealth.com)
- Service accounts for testing: thera-poc-bot@therahealth.com, thera-qa@therahealth.com — request TTL 48h
- No PHI in test vectors; we'll provide example tokens for your smoke suite.

Please send the peering request when ready and the ephemeral keys for the two service accounts so we can run the baseline sooner rather than later. Once the peering is up, we will run the smoke tests and post results to the MAP workbook and the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345).

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Platform Ops, TheraHealth
alex.rivera@therahealth.com
